data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'Ioseceline', meaning 'Jesus' little one' or 'God's little one'. In Christianity, Jocelina is a name for a girl associated with the Virgin Mary and Jesus. The name Jocelina carries the meaning “God's little one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Jocelina usually hope their child will grow to embody god's little one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolic of divine protection and devotion to the Christian faith.
data.etymology: Jocelina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's little one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jocelina total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Jocelina of Préaux, a Norman noblewoman and abbess, was widely revered for her piety and miracles. She is said to have lived from 1010 to 1070. Jocelina's father was Count Mauger II of Montreuil and her mother was Hedwige of Conteville. She was educated at the monastery of Montreuil-sur-Mer and entered religious life as a Benedictine nun around 1030. In 1050, she was appointed abbess of the priory of Préaux, which she governed until her death in 1070. Her relics were enshrined in a shrine and her cult continued to grow after her death.

Jocelina of Bobbio, an Italian Benedictine nun and abbess, is known for her advocacy for the canonization of Saint Columba of Bobbio. She lived in the 7th century. Jocelina was born into the noble Ligurian family of the Aliprandi. After the death of her husband, she entered the monastery of San Colombano at Bobbio around 617 and became a nun. She later became abbess of the monastery around 630. During her tenure as abbess, she oversaw the construction of the abbey church and the expansion of the monastery. She also played a significant role in the canonization process of Saint Columba of Bobbio, who was her spiritual guide and mentor.
